question: What does the 2014 Mandulog goby-fishery paper support about household fishing and gobies used as prey, and what cannot be treated as a direct fish-diet observation?

source.citation: Vedra, S. A., & Ocampo, P. P. (2014). The Fishery Potential of Freshwater Gobies in Mandulog River, Northern Mindanao, Philippines. Asian Journal of Agriculture and Development, 11(1), 95-103.
source.access: The official SEARCA AJAD article page and June 2014 issue listing were reviewed. The abstract and article metadata are readable. The publisher page offers a free PDF download through an interactive form protected by reCAPTCHA; the PDF was not retrieved in this review. The similarly named AgEcon Search direct PDF path redirected to an unrelated 2004 Ukrainian agriculture dissertation in this browsing environment, so that misdirected file was not used. No full-text statements beyond the publisher abstract are asserted here.

studyContext.waterbodyAsReported: Mandulog River, Iligan City, Northern Mindanao, Philippines.
studyContext.studyDesignAvailableFromAbstract: The abstract says households along the Mandulog River were respondents to a survey about the fishery potential of freshwater gobies. The abstract does not provide respondent count, survey date, barangay/reach allocation, questionnaire, or respondent-to-catch crosswalk.
historicalFisheryStatements: The abstract reports gobies caught for household food and goby fry sold in markets.
It reports fishing about five times per year using nets and traps.

The abstract reports a maximum catch of 1-3 kg per fishing session, around PHP 10/kg, and monthly income of PHP 100-200; these are historical abstract-level values with no denominator, uncertainty, or current applicability established here.
studyContext.coordinates: The reviewed abstract provides no station coordinates, datum/CRS, waterbody geometry, or sample-to-site table. No spatial feature was created.

respondentReportedPreyTaxa.sourcePhrase: The publisher abstract calls these gobies 'preferred prey species.'
respondentReportedPreyTaxa.evidenceType: Publisher-abstract summary of a household survey; the exact respondent question and whether 'preferred' means observed consumption, fisher choice, or another reported practice are not available in the reviewed abstract.
respondentReportedPreyTaxa.predatorIdentification: No predator fish species is identified in the publisher abstract. No gut-content, DNA, or direct predator-prey observation method is described there.
respondentReportedPreyTaxa.handling: Retain as a historical respondent/fishery lead that some Mandulog gobies were reported as prey; do not turn the gobies into universal bait recommendations or infer which named predatory fish eats them. Preserve source-name strings; no taxonomic crosswalk is made in this review.

relatedSources.relation: The 2013 article also includes community household interviews and fish sampling in Mandulog. It reports 273 interview respondents across upstream, midstream, and downstream reaches; the 2014 abstract only says households were respondents and gives no count or date. The shared lead author, river, and topic create a possible overlap, but no respondent, survey-form, or raw-data crosswalk is available here.

The SEARCA dissertation abstract describes a year-long goby study and reports matching seasonal/reach catch totals with the 2013 paper. The dissertation metadata abstract does not establish whether the 2014 fishery household survey is a separate sample or an overlapping questionnaire/data product.

The 2015 article reports direct gut-content work from fish collected in May-June 2014 at five sites. The 2014 fishery abstract instead describes household respondents. No sample or respondent crosswalk links these studies; do not pool their evidence or use the 2014 prey phrase to validate 2015 gut observations.

overlapAssessment.handling: Treat the household fishery study as a separate publication but do not count it as an independent survey sample from the 2012/2013 Mandulog community work without full methods, matching respondent details, or raw-source crosswalk.

interpretation.safeSummary: The 2014 AJAD abstract describes a household survey about Mandulog goby fisheries and names six goby source labels as 'preferred prey species.' This is a respondent-derived fishery statement with no predator species, respondent denominator, exact survey date, or direct diet method in the abstract. It is useful as a historical local lead, not as a confirmed predator-species diet card.
notSupported: A direct gut-content or observed feeding claim for any named predator fish.
A named predator-to-prey relation, because the abstract does not identify predator fish taxa.
A universal or species-wide diet, bait suggestion, catchability estimate, or catch guarantee.
Current goby abundance, fishery frequency, market prices, livelihood conditions, or present-day fishing rules.
Independent sample totals when combined with the 2012 dissertation, 2013 paper, or 2015 gut-content study.
A current occurrence, geometry, water-safety, access, or public species record.

qualityAndRights.evidenceLevel: Primary publisher abstract and bibliographic metadata reviewed; full article PDF and methods were not retrieved. Household-reported prey category is therefore not independently assessed.
qualityAndRights.reuseStatus: SEARCA AJAD's public page lists free PDF access. AJAD's publication ethics page states that article content may be quoted with credit but that an entire article may not be republished without written permission. No open license or project-specific republication permission was verified. Only a concise attributed research summary and links are retained.
qualityAndRights.safetyAndDietBoundary: Historical household/fishery reporting is separate from gut-content evidence, current fish presence, bait advice, legal fishing guidance, or safety assessment.

disposition.reason: The publisher abstract supports only a historical household-survey summary and a set of gobies called preferred prey species. It does not identify predators or describe direct diet methods, and the respondent sample relationship to related Mandulog studies is unresolved.

nextAction: The separate 2024 Mandulog fish-fauna survey is reviewed in national-mindanao-mandulog-2024-fish-fauna-survey-review-20261031.json. Next, cross-check its 14 source name forms against current taxonomic authorities; do not infer specimen identity, present-day occurrence, or a direct predator-prey relation from these separate papers.

sources.supports: Official SEARCA AJAD article page, publisher abstract, authors, issue date, pages, and free full-text download route.
Official June 2014 Volume 11 Issue 1 listing and the article's issue context.
Publisher's copyright statement about short attributed quotations and written permission for whole-article republication.
Official UPLB record for the 2013 Mandulog goby article used only to identify possible respondent-data overlap.
Official SEARCA dissertation abstract used to identify a possible overlapping Mandulog goby research program; it does not establish respondent overlap with the 2014 article.
MSU-IIT faculty publication record for the separate 2015 Mandulog gut-content article, used to distinguish its fish-sampling study from the 2014 household survey.
